## Context / Problem
Multiple production bugs (3435, 3a33, 4dd2, 4c6c class) came from store write paths that bypassed the canonical write seams with raw 'git add/commit/rm' — including inside GitHub workflow YAML (the real reconcile-bridge.yml bypass was `cd .tickets-tracker` + bare `git add -A` + `git commit`, .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml ~:285-291: the git line itself carries no tracker token; only the preceding cd targets it). The routing campaign fixed known sites; nothing prevents new bypasses. The REAL write surface has two sanctioned seams, not one: (1) the store seam — locked write transactions and event appends whose INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py run_git/run_git_write themselves, _store/event_append.py's own _run_git add/commit, _commands/txn.py's inline add/commit/reset critical section — the relocated ticket_txn; the old _engine/ticket_txn.py is deleted, so ticket_txn must NOT be named as an entry point —, _commands/purge_bridge.py's locked add -A + commit ~:154, and migration/bootstrap paths); and (2) the reconciler seam — _engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py (own add/commit/update-ref against TICKETS_REF) and _ref_lock.py (update-ref CAS acquire/release). NOTE: run_git_write is NOT the lock (it only self-heals index.lock/HEAD-parse faults); the unified store lock lives in the transaction/append layers above it, so the teaching message must direct authors to the store WRITE APIs, not bare run_git_write.

## Approach
Two-layer deterministic CI lint, each layer matched to what is statically decidable, with sanction via an INLINE MARKER carrying a mandatory reason — no external allowlist file. Marker: `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` (and `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` comment lines in YAML/shell). A new marker name rather than overloading the existing `# tickets-boundary-ok` convention, because the semantics differ (boundary-crossing READ/layout sanction vs raw WRITE sanction) — the plan states this reconciliation explicitly; marker-without-reason fails the lint. Layer P (Python, AST), TWO rules matched to the codebase's two real write shapes: R1 — any RAW subprocess invocation whose argv carries git plus a mutation verb (add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean), where the argv is resolved by LOCAL INTRA-FUNCTION TRACKING, not literal-only matching: a list literal inline at the call, a local variable assigned a list literal (including subsequent .append/.extend of literals) in the same function body, or — fail-closed — an OPAQUE argv (a bare parameter or non-literal expression), which fires as 'unresolvable argv' and is sanctioned only by the marker (the wrapper-internal bodies gitutil.run_git and event_append._run_git are exactly this shape and receive their seam-internal marker). The raw sites at HEAD are few and verified: the shared wrapper INTERNALS (gitutil.run_git's subprocess.run, event_append._run_git ~:245-256, _ref_lock._git ~:244-252) plus _commands/txn.py's inline reset ~:143 and _commands/purge_bridge.py's add/commit ~:153-158. R2 — any CALL to the shared git wrappers BY NAME (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git — the four wrapper names at HEAD, listed in the lint) passing a mutation verb resolved by the SAME intra-function tracking as R1: (a) a string literal anywhere in the call's arguments INCLUDING nested list literals (`_git(["update-ref", ref, new]）` — the _ref_lock CAS caller shape; txn.py run_git_write(...,'add'...) ~:128), (b) a local list variable built from literals then passed plain or SPLATTED (`args = ["commit"]; ... run_git(_root(repo_root), *args)` — the shape git_adapter.commit/update_ref/rm_cached actually use, git_adapter.py ~:171-251, and `argv = [..."commit"...]; _run_git(argv)` — event_append._git_commit_paths ~:319-337), or (c) fail-closed, an OPAQUE argv (a bare parameter forwarded to a wrapper name, e.g. _ref_lock._git's own body forwarding `*args` to run_git ~:244-272), which fires as 'unresolvable argv to git wrapper' and takes the delegation-seam marker. Literal-only matching would miss (b) and (c) — the codebase's OWN idiom builds the verb into a local list before the call, so a future bypass author copying that idiom must not stay green. Both rules suppressed only by the marker on the line or enclosing function. Rationale for module-agnostic flagging: rebar's Python writes git only for the tracker/its mirrors OR for DISPOSABLE SANDBOX repos (two known sites: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py _git_init/add/commit fixture repos ~:27-44, src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py _git_init + fixture add/commit ~:352-415) — so every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass. ALL of them get flagged by default and the first two categories carry the marker (`# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` / `# raw-git-ok: disposable sandbox repo, not the tracker`); no tracker-targeting dataflow analysis needed, which is exactly what makes the lint deterministic. The sandbox sites are enumerated in the first-scan marker list alongside the seam internals. Layer W (workflows + shell, cwd-aware within-step): parse .github/workflows/*.yml run-blocks and scripts/*.sh; flag a git mutation verb ONLY when the same step/script block establishes tracker context — `cd` into a path containing the tracker dir name (.tickets-tracker), `git -C <tracker-path>`, or a `working-directory:` naming it — the exact reconcile-bridge.yml shape. Ordinary repo commits in workflows (docs/artifacts) never fire (no tracker context). ACCEPTED RESIDUAL (stated in the lint header + docs): argv construction that crosses function boundaries or is computed dynamically (beyond the local intra-function list tracking) resolves as the fail-closed opaque-argv class when it reaches a wrapper name or raw subprocess, and tracker targeting laundered through a variable in Layer W remains undetectable statically; the lint deterministically catches the literal, local-variable/splat, and opaque-forwarding shapes — which cover every historical bypass and the codebase's own write idioms. First full scan: mark the enumerated R1 raw sites and R2 seam-internal wrapper calls above with reasons (NOTE: _store/lock.py needs NO marker — it locks via fcntl/mkdir and only RESOLVES git paths, issuing no git subprocess); remediate or mark any other hit. Failure message teaches: 'store writes go through the event-append/transaction APIs (rebar.tickets / _store.event_append / _commands.txn) or the reconciler git_adapter; if this raw write is genuinely seam-internal, add # raw-git-ok: <reason>'. Pattern precedent: module-size gate (deterministic scan, teaching error) + check_*.py script convention wired into _build-and-test.yml.

## Scope
- new lint script scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py (Layer P + Layer W in one script, check()/main() convention, EXCLUDED self-fixtures) + CI wiring as a named step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml
- inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)
- remediation of any additional bypass sites the first full scan finds
- docs: one paragraph in the contributing/store docs naming the sanctioned write seams and the marker

## Testing
Lint unit tests: (P) raw `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", t, "commit", ...])` in an unmarked module fails with the teaching message; same line with `# raw-git-ok: reason` passes; marker WITHOUT reason fails; git read verbs (status/log/rev-parse) never fire; VARIABLE-ARGV: `args = ["commit", "-m", m]; run_git(root, *args)` and `argv = ["git", "-C", t, "commit"]; _run_git(argv)` both fire via the intra-function tracking, a local list carrying only a read verb (`["log"]`) does not fire, and an OPAQUE argv (bare parameter forwarded to a wrapper name) fires fail-closed and is silenced by the marker. (W) a workflow step with `cd .tickets-tracker` + bare `git add -A` fails; `git -C .tickets-tracker commit` fails; a bare `git commit` step with NO tracker context passes (the docs-commit false-positive control); `working-directory: .tickets-tracker` + git mutation fails. Self-exclusion: the lint's own test fixtures are excluded (EXCLUDED_FILES tuple, check_criteria_vocabulary.py:38 idiom). Full-tree run is clean at merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CI fails on unmarked raw git mutations in rebar Python (module-agnostic) and on tracker-context git mutations in workflows/shell (cwd-aware within-step), with the teaching message naming the store write APIs and the reconciler seam.
- [ ] Sanction is a single inline marker with mandatory reason; marker-without-reason fails; relationship to the existing tickets-boundary-ok convention documented.
- [ ] All enumerated seam internals (both seams) are marked with reasons; tree is clean at landing; the reconcile-bridge.yml historical shape is covered by a failing test fixture.
- [ ] Lint has its own unit tests including the no-tracker-context negative control, the variable-argv positive cases (splat and plain local-list argv: the git_adapter.commit/update_ref/rm_cached and event_append._git_commit_paths shapes fire), the opaque-argv fail-closed case (_ref_lock._git delegation shape), and the remaining accepted residual (CROSS-function/dynamic argv construction beyond intra-function tracking) documented in the lint header.
